newsitem.title: CHILE: Chuquicamata supervisors to discuss pay offer.
newsitem.headline: Chuquicamata supervisors to discuss pay offer.

text.p: Supervisors at Codelco's Chuquicamata pit will meet later Monday in a meeting to discuss the Chilean state copper company's final offer made Friday in scheduled wage talks, a Chuquicamata spokesman said.

The 700-odd supervisors will vote on the offer in a ballot scheduled to last most of Tuesday, the spokesman said. He said management had agreed with the union to make no comment on the content of the negotiations or their chances of success while talks lasted.
No union spokesman was immediately available for comment.
Last Friday, a source close to the bargaining told Reuters Friday that the chances of a vote to accept the offer were good.
Talks were concentrating on several points including health benefits and bonuses, the source said.
If the supervisors vote to reject the offer, Chilean law requires five days pass in which both sides can try to find a solution to the disagreement before a strike can legally begin.
Chuquicamata's 7,000 miners went on strike for 10 days last year after scheduled wage talks broke down.
The mine, the largest of Codelco's four mining divisions, produced 632,000 tonnes of fine copper in 1996.
